22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222.history: MIT was chartered by Massachusetts in 1861 on a plan put forward by geologist William Barton Rogers, held its first classes in Boston in 1865, and moved across the Charles River to Cambridge in 1916. It was built around laboratory-based, applied teaching, reflected in its motto 'mind and hand'. It is now a private research university organised into five schools plus the Schwarzman College of Computing, founded in 2019.

sources.label: Official MIT Facts: founded 1861, Cambridge move 1916, motto, campus

5ad45ea9-e51c-59e4-9ef7-6d3768be673c.history: Imperial College was created by royal charter in 1907, bringing together the Royal College of Science, the Royal School of Mines and the City and Guilds College in South Kensington. During the 20th century it absorbed several London medical schools, including St Mary's Hospital Medical School in 1988, and in 2007 it left the federal University of London to become fully independent. It focuses on science, engineering, medicine and business across several campuses in London and the South East.
5ad45ea9-e51c-59e4-9ef7-6d3768be673c.motto: Scientia imperii decus et tutamen (Knowledge is the adornment and protection of the Empire)

sources.label: Official About page: founded 1907 in South Kensington, nine campuses

11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111.history: Leland and Jane Stanford founded the university in 1885 in memory of their son, and it opened to students in 1891 on the couple's former stock farm near Palo Alto, California. Its research growth after the Second World War, including Stanford Research Park in the early 1950s, tied it closely to the rise of Silicon Valley. It is a private research university with seven schools, among them engineering, medicine, law, business and the Doerr School of Sustainability.
11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111.motto: Die Luft der Freiheit weht (The wind of freedom blows)

sources.label: Official Stanford Facts: founded 1885 (input 1891 is the opening year), 7,289 undergraduates + 10,025 graduate students, Autumn 2025 (total is the sum)

33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333.history: Oxford has no exact founding date, but teaching was under way by 1096, and the university grew quickly after 1167, when Henry II stopped English students from attending the University of Paris. It is a collegiate university of more than 30 self-governing colleges and several permanent private halls, and undergraduate teaching centres on small-group tutorials. Women were admitted to full membership of the university in 1920.
33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333.motto: Dominus illuminatio mea (The Lord is my light)

sources.label: Official facts page (blocked to WebFetch, read via an alternative extractor): 12,460 undergraduates + 13,755 postgraduates; 43% international as of 1 Dec 2025. Founding year 1096 is the earliest evidence of teaching, not a charter date

39230496-b2fc-53ca-9303-1726c4ac13da.history: Harvard was founded in 1636 by a vote of the Great and General Court of the Massachusetts Bay Colony, making it the oldest college in what became the United States. It was named after John Harvard, a minister who left the college his library and half of his estate. Over the 19th and 20th centuries it grew into a university with graduate and professional schools in Cambridge and Boston.

sources.label: Official About page: founding 28 Oct 1636 by the Massachusetts Bay Colony, John Harvard bequest
Official Fact Book: 24,317 distinct students, fall 2025; 6,749 U.S. nonresident (percentage computed from these counts)

ae117645-e24c-5269-8ed1-b5b826e53932.history: The university grew out of a group of scholars who left Oxford for Cambridge in 1209, and its oldest college, Peterhouse, was founded in 1284. It is a collegiate university of 31 colleges, which house students and run small-group teaching called supervisions, while faculties and departments give lectures and carry out research. Its scientific history includes Isaac Newton and the Cavendish Laboratory, which opened in the 1870s.
ae117645-e24c-5269-8ed1-b5b826e53932.motto: Hinc lucem et pocula sacra (From here, light and sacred draughts)

sources.label: Official 'Cambridge at a glance': founded 1209; 24,927 students (12,850 UG, 12,080 PG), 2025-26; 31 colleges

6020a2b5-3788-5dd1-b3f2-b9c6c7c6f99b.history: ETH Zurich opened in 1855 as the Swiss Federal Polytechnic School, created by the new federal state under an 1854 law, and took its current name in 1911. It is run by the Swiss Confederation within the ETH Domain, alongside EPFL and four federal research institutes. Albert Einstein studied and later taught there.

sources.label: Official portrait page: origins in 1855, federal institution, Einstein

99fbcf31-606d-5dac-880e-83ca25acd942.history: Caltech began in 1891 as Throop University, a small school in Pasadena founded by local businessman and politician Amos G. Throop, and was renamed the California Institute of Technology in 1920. Astronomer George Ellery Hale, physicist Robert Millikan and chemist Arthur Amos Noyes turned it into a research-focused institute in the 1910s and 1920s. It is very small by enrollment and manages NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, which grew out of Caltech rocket research in the 1930s.
99fbcf31-606d-5dac-880e-83ca25acd942.motto: The truth shall make you free

sources.label: Official 'At a glance': founded 1891 as Throop University, renamed 1920; 971 undergraduates + 1,398 graduate students (total is the sum; no year stated); JPL

c66c3755-66a2-57a0-a80e-da984c310d29.history: NUS traces its origins to a medical school that opened in 1905 with 23 students, funded by local businessmen led by Tan Jiak Kim. That school combined with Raffles College in 1949 to form the University of Malaya, whose Singapore campus later became the University of Singapore, and the present NUS was created in 1980 when the University of Singapore merged with Nanyang University. It now has three campuses, at Kent Ridge, Bukit Timah and Outram.

sources.label: Official About page: founded 1905 with 23 students (Tan Jiak Kim); about 29,300 UG + 16,400 graduate students, AY2025/26 (rounded); three campuses. Read via an alternative extractor because WebFetch returned an empty page

4b7862dc-7567-5f81-af58-c01144412a88.history: UCL was founded in 1826 as London University, a secular alternative to Oxford and Cambridge that admitted students regardless of their religion, and in 1878 it began admitting women on equal terms with men. It became a founding college of the University of London in 1836 and gained university status in its own right in 2023. It is a large multi-faculty university centred on Bloomsbury in central London.
4b7862dc-7567-5f81-af58-c01144412a88.motto: Cuncti adsint meritaeque expectent praemia palmae (Let all come who by merit most deserve the reward)

sources.label: Wikipedia (official facts page blocked/404): history, motto. Student totals not set because official figures conflicted (a search snippet gave 51,793 in 2024/25 with 52% from abroad; the official study pages say 18,000 from outside the UK)

b37d730b-421c-5ed6-a807-3d66e7ca21f7.history: HKU was incorporated in 1911 and admitted its first students in 1912. It took in the Hong Kong College of Medicine for Chinese, founded in 1887, whose early students included Sun Yat-sen. It is the oldest university in Hong Kong, teaches mainly in English, and has its main campus on the western side of Hong Kong Island.
b37d730b-421c-5ed6-a807-3d66e7ca21f7.motto: Sapientia et Virtus; 明德格物 (Wisdom and Virtue)

sources.label: Official history: 1887 College of Medicine, 1911 incorporation, 1912 first students
Official QuickStats: 45,303 headcount (2025/26); 55.3% non-local by nationality. Non-local includes Mainland Chinese students, so this is not strictly 'international'

f5a6d73a-5fd2-55de-83af-3da2c25e18ef.history: NTU's roots lie in Nanyang University, a Chinese-medium university opened in 1955, and in the Nanyang Technological Institute, set up on 8 August 1981 to train engineers for Singapore. The institute was reconstituted as Nanyang Technological University on 1 July 1991 and absorbed the National Institute of Education, Singapore's teacher-training institution. It now covers engineering, science, business, humanities and medicine on its main campus in western Singapore.

sources.label: Official history: Nanyang University 1955, NTI 1981, NTU inaugurated 1 July 1991 incorporating NIE
Official facts page: figures only as images, so no student total recorded

7add53a9-8ddf-5e84-bd4d-a7c8638dbb95.history: The University of Chicago was incorporated in 1890 by the American Baptist Education Society with major funding from John D. Rockefeller, and it opened in 1892 under its first president, William Rainey Harper. Physicists there achieved the first controlled nuclear chain reaction in 1942. It is known for the Core curriculum in its undergraduate College and for influential schools of thought in economics, sociology and law.
7add53a9-8ddf-5e84-bd4d-a7c8638dbb95.motto: Crescat scientia; vita excolatur (Let knowledge grow from more to more; and so be human life enriched)

sources.label: Official institutional data: total enrollment 19,140, Fall 2025

79e1cf8b-6a97-5fef-ac23-aa6012197801.history: Peking University was founded in 1898 as the Imperial University of Peking during the late-Qing reform movement, as China's first modern national university, and was renamed Peking University in 1912. Under president Cai Yuanpei from 1917 it became a centre of the New Culture and May Fourth movements. In 1952 it moved to the former Yenching University campus, Yan Yuan, in north-west Beijing, and in 2000 it merged with Beijing Medical University.

sources.label: Official About page: founded 1898 as Imperial University of Peking; 46,113 full-time students (facts last updated Dec 2020). The international figure was not used because the page gives two conflicting numbers

519c66df-8779-5336-acda-2cba10f95c66.history: Tsinghua opened in 1911 as Tsing Hua Imperial College, a preparatory school, funded with returned Boxer Indemnity money, for students going to study in the United States. It became National Tsing Hua University in 1928, and during the war with Japan it joined Peking and Nankai universities to form the National Southwest Associated University in Kunming. After China's 1952 restructuring it became mainly a polytechnic training engineers, and it has since rebuilt programmes in the sciences, humanities, economics and management.
519c66df-8779-5336-acda-2cba10f95c66.motto: 自强不息，厚德载物 (Self-discipline and Social Commitment)

sources.label: Official facts: 63,132 registered students (data by 2025-12-31); 784+1,397+450 international (percentage computed from these counts)

894119e1-40c1-5589-8677-e1ed97388e59.history: Penn dates its origins to 1740, and Benjamin Franklin led its early board of trustees and promoted a curriculum that combined practical and classical subjects; regular classes began in the early 1750s. It opened the first medical school in the American colonies in 1765 and, in 1881, the Wharton School, the first collegiate business school. Its main campus is in the University City area of West Philadelphia.
894119e1-40c1-5589-8677-e1ed97388e59.motto: Leges sine moribus vanae (Laws without morals are useless)

sources.label: Official Penn Facts: history dates to 1740; 29,384 students, Fall 2025; 6,785 international (percentage computed from these counts)

8488d97e-a227-5fbd-b7b4-33a1194df723.history: Cornell was founded in 1865 by Ezra Cornell and Andrew Dickson White and opened in Ithaca, New York, in 1868 as a nonsectarian university open to students regardless of background. It is New York's federal land-grant institution, and several of its colleges are state-supported statutory colleges, so it has both private and public functions. Besides the Ithaca campus, it runs Weill Cornell Medicine and Cornell Tech in New York City and a medical college in Qatar.
8488d97e-a227-5fbd-b7b4-33a1194df723.motto: I would found an institution where any person can find instruction in any study

sources.label: Official About page: founded 1865, land-grant, locations; 16,138 undergraduates + 10,423 graduate/professional students (total is the sum; no year stated)

0a670c6d-e20a-527f-851b-e2c1306cce70.history: Yale was chartered by the Connecticut colony in 1701 as the Collegiate School, moved to New Haven in 1716, and was renamed in 1718 after the merchant Elihu Yale gave it goods and books. In 1861 it awarded the first PhD degrees in the United States, and in the 1930s it set up its residential college system for undergraduates. Today it combines Yale College with graduate and professional schools, including law, medicine, drama and art.

sources.label: Official Yale Facts (2025 data): 15,657 students, 3,824 international (24%)

e67501b3-2e87-5598-b9e3-e28fe4101f68.history: UC Berkeley was established by the California Legislature in 1868, when the private College of California merged with a planned state land-grant college, and it moved to its Berkeley site in 1873. It is the oldest campus of the University of California system. Its researchers are linked to the discovery of many chemical elements, and it manages Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory.

sources.label: Official 'By the numbers': 33,070 undergraduates + 12,812 graduate students, Fall 2024 (total is the sum)

7deae08f-080e-56cd-8aa8-ca05c941f0cc.history: CUHK was established in 1963 by joining three existing post-secondary colleges: Chung Chi College, New Asia College and United College. It was set up as a bilingual university teaching in Chinese and English, and it keeps a collegiate system that has grown to nine colleges. Its main campus is on a hillside in Sha Tin in the New Territories.
7deae08f-080e-56cd-8aa8-ca05c941f0cc.motto: 博文約禮 (Through learning and temperance to virtue)

sources.label: Official Facts & Figures: counts cover only publicly funded programmes, so no total recorded

6f8ca7da-1cba-56f4-89e6-4cffd48126ac.history: The University of Melbourne was established by an act of the Victorian colonial parliament in 1853 and began teaching at Parkville, just north of the city centre, in 1855. It is Australia's second-oldest university. In 2008 it introduced the 'Melbourne Model', under which professional fields such as law and medicine are taught at graduate level after a broad undergraduate degree.
6f8ca7da-1cba-56f4-89e6-4cffd48126ac.motto: Postera crescam laude (I shall grow in the esteem of future generations)

sources.label: Official 2024 Annual Report 'At a glance': 77,162 students (headcount). Direct fetch blocked (403); figure read from the search index of this page

34f9bd5c-1c24-5d4f-880c-4a342627a148.history: UNSW was founded in 1949 as the New South Wales University of Technology, set up to train engineers and scientists for post-war industry, and took its current name in 1958. It has since grown into a comprehensive university, with its main campus at Kensington in Sydney's eastern suburbs. It also teaches in Canberra, including at the Australian Defence Force Academy.
34f9bd5c-1c24-5d4f-880c-4a342627a148.motto: Scientia manu et mente (Knowledge by hand and mind)

sources.label: Official 'Our story': founded 1949; '63,232+ students' (no year stated); four main campuses

f5c17f3c-ac83-5193-8c71-641147ad926c.history: Johns Hopkins opened in Baltimore in 1876, funded by a bequest from the merchant Johns Hopkins. Under its first president, Daniel Coit Gilman, it was modelled on German research universities and emphasised graduate study. Its School of Medicine, opened in 1893, admitted women from the start and required a prior degree, and it influenced the shape of modern American medical education.
f5c17f3c-ac83-5193-8c71-641147ad926c.motto: Veritas vos liberabit (The truth will set you free)

sources.label: Wikipedia (official jhu.edu pages blocked with 403): history, motto

819bd7c2-cc38-5dc4-854d-2d59a8a9f4e5.history: EPFL traces its origins to the École spéciale de Lausanne, a private engineering school founded in 1853 that later became part of the University of Lausanne. In 1969 it was separated from the university and became a federal institute of technology run by the Swiss Confederation, alongside ETH Zurich. Its campus at Ecublens, on the shore of Lake Geneva, includes an innovation park for start-ups and company research labs.

44444444-4444-4444-8444-444444444444.history: TUM was founded in 1868 by King Ludwig II of Bavaria as the Polytechnic School in Munich, became a technical college of university rank in 1877, and took the name Technische Universität München in 1970. It has expanded from its city-centre site to large campuses at Garching and at Weihenstephan in Freising, plus a site in Heilbronn. It covers engineering, natural sciences, medicine, life sciences and management.

sources.label: Official 'TUM in figures': 51,954 students (winter semester 2025/26, as of 1 Dec 2025); 45% international

6f13f9e9-cf5f-56ad-8384-39a9dc592d58.history: Princeton was chartered in 1746 as the College of New Jersey, held its first classes in Elizabeth and then Newark, and moved to Princeton in 1756, where Nassau Hall became its main building. It was renamed Princeton University in 1896. It is a private research university with a strong undergraduate focus and has no medical, law or business school.
6f13f9e9-cf5f-56ad-8384-39a9dc592d58.motto: Dei sub numine viget (Under God's power she flourishes)

sources.label: Wikipedia (official facts page blocked with 403): history, motto. Enrollment not set because only partial figures from different pages were available

c67598f4-8b91-53a9-a98a-ebd185ced219.history: The University of Sydney was founded in 1850 by an act of the New South Wales colonial legislature, making it Australia's first university, and it began teaching in 1852. Its main Camperdown/Darlington campus in inner Sydney is known for the sandstone Quadrangle, begun in the 1850s. It admitted women to degrees from 1881.
c67598f4-8b91-53a9-a98a-ebd185ced219.motto: Sidere mens eadem mutato (Though the stars change, the mind is the same)

sources.label: Official About page: '175 years', '70,000+ students' (approximate, no year, so not recorded)

5c9532a7-118a-5e2d-ab32-92ade2e776a5.history: Fudan was established in Shanghai in 1905 as Fudan Public School, led by Ma Xiangbo, who had earlier founded Zhendan (Aurora) Academy, and it took the name Fudan University in 1917. It was named one of China's national key universities in 1959 and merged with Shanghai Medical University in 2000. Its main campus is on Handan Road in Shanghai's Yangpu District.
5c9532a7-118a-5e2d-ab32-92ade2e776a5.motto: 博学而笃志，切问而近思 (Study widely and hold firm to your aims; question earnestly and reflect on what is near)

sources.label: Official About page: est. 1905, renamed 1917, 2000 merger; 13,623 UG/associate + 22,610 graduate students as of 1 May 2019 (total is the sum)

b48ecdd6-9331-5ee8-a4ad-7f5b046d5356.history: McGill was founded under a royal charter granted in 1821, using land and money left by the Montreal merchant James McGill, who died in 1813. Its Faculty of Medicine, established in 1829, was the first in Canada. It teaches mainly in English, with a downtown Montreal campus at the foot of Mount Royal and the Macdonald campus in Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue.
b48ecdd6-9331-5ee8-a4ad-7f5b046d5356.motto: Grandescunt aucta labore (By work, all things increase and grow)

sources.label: Official Quick Facts: 40,531 total students (Fall 2025); 27% international by place of origin; Faculty of Medicine 1829

c5ca35b6-8983-574d-89ec-d15da6afa1fe.history: PSL was founded in 2010 as a grouping of Parisian grandes écoles and national research institutions, and it later became a single public university. Its member schools include the École normale supérieure, Mines Paris, Université Paris Dauphine, ESPCI Paris, Chimie ParisTech and the Observatoire de Paris, and the Collège de France and Institut Curie are associated institutions. Its teaching and research take place at several sites, mostly in central Paris.

sources.label: Official PSL page: founded 2010; member schools; '17,000' students (rounded, no year)

55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555.history: The University of Toronto was chartered in 1827 as King's College, an Anglican institution, and became the non-denominational University of Toronto in 1850. It developed as a federation of colleges, including Trinity, Victoria and St. Michael's, and now has three campuses: St. George in downtown Toronto, Mississauga and Scarborough. Insulin was discovered there in 1921–22.
55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555.motto: Velut arbor aevo (As a tree with the passage of time)

sources.label: Official Quick facts: 102,431 students incl. 29,449 international (Fall 2024-25; percentage computed). Direct fetch failed (connection reset); figures read from the search index of this page

14fa4c62-b910-520b-aa51-0bf334f02b1c.history: ANU was created by an act of the Australian Parliament in 1946 as a national, research-only university in Canberra, and it began undergraduate teaching after it merged with Canberra University College in 1960. It runs the Mount Stromlo and Siding Spring observatories through its Research School of Astronomy and Astrophysics. It is known for research on Asia and the Pacific and on public policy.
14fa4c62-b910-520b-aa51-0bf334f02b1c.motto: Naturam primum cognoscere rerum (First to learn the nature of things)

sources.label: Official 'Facts about ANU': founded 1946; 10,252 UG + 7,128 PG students (total is the sum; no year stated)

01649f44-22e4-5b85-adaa-81f3538aa083.history: King's College London was founded in 1829 with the backing of King George IV and the Duke of Wellington, as a Church of England counterpart to the secular London University (now UCL). It became a founding college of the University of London in 1836 and later grew through mergers, including with the Guy's and St Thomas' medical and dental schools in 1998. It gained university status in its own right in 2023 and has several campuses near the Thames in central London.
01649f44-22e4-5b85-adaa-81f3538aa083.motto: Sancte et sapienter (With holiness and wisdom)

sources.label: Official 'Our students' page (updated Oct 2026): 45,914 students; 21,263 overseas (46.3%). Its subtotals do not add up exactly to the headline figure

66cc3fd0-3055-5d88-b1d0-586a11515643.history: Monash was established by an act of the Victorian Parliament in 1958, named after the engineer and First World War commander Sir John Monash, and took its first students at Clayton in 1961. It grew through mergers in the 1990s and now has several campuses in and around Melbourne, plus campuses in Malaysia and Indonesia. It has a large international student body and a broad range of faculties.

sources.label: Wikipedia (official facts pages blocked with 403): history, motto. Enrollment not set because the only official figure seen was a 'student load', not a headcount

74996b5e-c39f-52f1-9e01-88f3051f155b.history: HKUST was set up by a Hong Kong ordinance in the late 1980s and admitted its first students in October 1991 at its campus overlooking Clear Water Bay. It was founded to support Hong Kong's shift towards a technology- and business-based economy, and it teaches in English. In 2022 it opened a second campus, HKUST (Guangzhou), in mainland China.

sources.label: Official Facts & Figures: 21,985 students as of Sep 2026; 11,356 non-local (percentage computed). Non-local includes Mainland Chinese students

f2f2a71c-abeb-5dc7-b18b-aa8b00611b0a.history: Edinburgh was founded by the town council under a royal charter from James VI in 1582, and teaching began in 1583, making it the youngest of Scotland's four ancient universities. In the 18th century it was a centre of the Scottish Enlightenment and of medical education. It merged with Edinburgh College of Art in 2011 and has sites across the city.

sources.label: Official Student Factsheet 2025/26: 48,820 students matriculated during the session (peak count 44,610)
Official 'Our History': royal charter 1582, teaching from 1583

6e2ae583-50c4-53d5-a0ed-d11422c64773.history: The University of Manchester traces its origins to the Manchester Mechanics' Institute of 1824 and to Owens College, founded in 1851. Owens College developed into the Victoria University of Manchester, and the Mechanics' Institute became UMIST; the two merged in 2004 to form the present university. Work done there includes Ernest Rutherford's research on the atomic nucleus and the isolation of graphene in 2004.

sources.label: Wikipedia (official facts page 404): 1824/1851 origins, 2004 merger, motto. Founding year 1824 is the earliest predecessor; the current legal entity dates from 2004

11087dc1-5405-5bd2-a5e2-def936b94cf7.history: The University of Tokyo was founded in 1877 by merging earlier government schools for Western learning and medicine, and in 1886 it became the first of Japan's Imperial Universities. It was called Tokyo Imperial University from 1897 and took its current name after the Second World War. Its main campuses are Hongo and Komaba in central Tokyo, along with Kashiwa in Chiba Prefecture.

sources.label: Wikipedia (official English facts pages returned 404 or connection reset): history, campuses

40dc3bce-f456-577e-9003-9c143d3b52bb.history: SJTU traces its roots to Nanyang College, founded in Shanghai in 1896 by Sheng Xuanhuai, which became part of Chiao Tung University after a merger in 1921. In the mid-1950s most of the university moved to Xi'an, and the Shanghai branch became the independent Shanghai Jiao Tong University in 1959. In 2005 it merged with Shanghai Second Medical University, which became its School of Medicine.
40dc3bce-f456-577e-9003-9c143d3b52bb.motto: 饮水思源，爱国荣校 (When you drink water, remember its source; love the country and bring honour to the school)

sources.label: Official history: 1896 Nanyang College, 1921, 1955 Xi'an move, 1959, 2005 medical merger

1ad9abe1-60cd-55ec-b227-5c8001db0475.history: Columbia was chartered in 1754 as King's College under King George II, and it reopened as Columbia College in 1784 after the American Revolution. It moved to its current Morningside Heights campus in Manhattan in 1897. It is a private research university that administers the Pulitzer Prizes and is affiliated with Barnard College.
1ad9abe1-60cd-55ec-b227-5c8001db0475.motto: In lumine Tuo videbimus lumen (In Thy light shall we see light)

6a9e2556-fc5f-56a2-bca0-9364f099818c.history: SNU was established in 1946 by bringing together ten higher education institutions in and around Seoul, and it opened that October with nine colleges and a graduate school. From 1975 most of its units moved to the Gwanak campus in southern Seoul. In December 2011 it changed from a government institution into an incorporated national university.
6a9e2556-fc5f-56a2-bca0-9364f099818c.motto: Veritas lux mea (The truth is my light)

sources.label: Official timeline: opened 15 Oct 1946, Gwanak move 1975, incorporation 2011

276cad09-4a66-51a1-9071-c1ffe923a508.history: UBC was established by provincial law in 1908, began teaching in 1915, and moved to its permanent Point Grey campus in Vancouver in 1925. A second campus, UBC Okanagan in Kelowna, opened in 2005. The Vancouver campus hosts TRIUMF, Canada's particle accelerator centre, which UBC runs with other universities.

sources.label: Official UBC Facts: 72,100 total students (no year stated); international shares are given only per campus

c0386da4-95a0-567a-8f70-81b33c5c7f06.history: UQ was established by an act of the Queensland Parliament in 1909 as the state's first university, and it began teaching in 1911 in Brisbane's Old Government House. From the late 1930s it moved to its main St Lucia campus, centred on the sandstone Great Court. It also has campuses at Gatton and Herston, and its researchers helped develop the technology behind the HPV (cervical cancer) vaccine.
c0386da4-95a0-567a-8f70-81b33c5c7f06.motto: Scientia ac labore (By means of knowledge and hard work)

sources.label: Official UQ Statistics: 60,193 students in 2025, 39.7% international

9f3cf72f-ca1e-5831-b48d-e5747fb631d6.history: Institut Polytechnique de Paris was created in 2019 as a public institution grouping École polytechnique, ENSTA Paris, ENSAE Paris, Télécom Paris and Télécom SudParis, which had left the Paris-Saclay university project; the official site now also lists École des Ponts among its founding schools. Its schools are concentrated on the Saclay plateau around Palaiseau, south of Paris. It focuses on engineering, applied mathematics, economics and digital technology.

sources.label: Official Facts and figures: 11,300 students, 54% international (no year stated); founding schools

e48a723c-68b4-560e-b4a0-09be01682853.history: Northwestern was founded in 1851 by a group of Methodist leaders, including John Evans, to serve the former Northwest Territory, and it began classes in 1855 in Evanston, on Lake Michigan just north of Chicago. Its medical and law schools are on a second campus in downtown Chicago, and it has a branch campus in Doha, Qatar. It is known for journalism, communication, management and engineering.

It is a private research university in Seoul's Seongbuk District with a second campus in Sejong.

e0088a48-e57b-58d4-bf07-2021931bc1a9.history: The University of Amsterdam grew out of the Athenaeum Illustre, which opened on 8 January 1632 with lectures by Gerardus Vossius and Caspar Barlaeus. It is now a large public research university spread across several sites in Amsterdam.

Alexander Graham Bell taught there while developing the telephone, and in 1877 Helen Magill White earned the first PhD awarded to a woman by an American university at BU.

b7e728a7-1aa5-5bce-badf-5ecb3a6ec992.history: Freie Universität Berlin was founded in West Berlin on 4 December 1948 by students and academics, with American support, after protests against political control of the University of Berlin in the Soviet sector. Its founding statutes gave students a role in governance, and historian Friedrich Meinecke was its first president. Its main campus is in the Dahlem district.

0aeeb18a-3be5-5bb9-9875-0bf4ce24d102.history: Nanjing University traces its origins to Sanjiang Normal School, founded in 1902. The school went through several names, including National Southeastern University and National Central University, before becoming Nanjing University in 1950. In the 1952 national restructuring it merged with Jinling University (the University of Nanking) and moved to the Gulou site. It is a member of China's C9 League of research universities.

e2e9494c-968c-55f4-8889-2ec1ac65fbdd.history: The University of Copenhagen opened in 1479 under King Christian I, following a papal bull of 1475. It was dissolved during the Reformation around 1531 and re-established by Christian III in 1537. British bombardment in 1807 destroyed most of its buildings, and in 2007 it absorbed Denmark's agricultural and pharmaceutical universities. It has campuses in Copenhagen and Frederiksberg.
e2e9494c-968c-55f4-8889-2ec1ac65fbdd.motto: Coelestem adspicit lucem (It beholds the celestial light)

b186f041-f090-5f21-b68a-5b22175d4b14.history: The University of Osaka was founded in 1931 as Osaka Imperial University, Japan's sixth imperial university, with schools of medicine and science, and physicist Hantaro Nagaoka was its first president. It regards the merchant academy Kaitokudo (1724) and Ogata Koan's Tekijuku school of Western medicine (1838) as its intellectual roots. It merged with Osaka University of Foreign Studies in 2007 and changed its English name to The University of Osaka in 2025.
b186f041-f090-5f21-b68a-5b22175d4b14.motto: 地域に生き世界に伸びる (Live Locally, Grow Globally)

74effccc-395b-52fb-8f50-2523f7897428.history: The University of Alberta was chartered under the provincial University Act of 1906, sponsored by Premier Alexander Rutherford, and began teaching in 1908 with 45 students under president Henry Marshall Tory. It awarded its first degrees in 1912 and added medicine and agriculture faculties soon after. Its Calgary branch became the independent University of Calgary in 1966.

0bfd2121-ebb3-562f-ad36-d6a5bf570d8b.history: The University of Nottingham began as a civic university college that opened in Nottingham city centre in 1881. The college moved in 1928 to University Park, on land given by Sir Jesse Boot, and became a degree-awarding university by royal charter in 1948. It opened the UK's first new medical school of the 20th century in 1970, and later campuses in Malaysia (2000) and Ningbo, China (2004).
0bfd2121-ebb3-562f-ad36-d6a5bf570d8b.motto: Sapientia urbs conditur (A city is built on wisdom)

1789110d-d2fe-546a-bb76-da8fc3c966d6.history: Institute of Science Tokyo was formed on 1 October 2024 by merging Tokyo Institute of Technology, which traces its roots to the Tokyo Vocational School of 1881, with Tokyo Medical and Dental University, founded as a dental school in 1928. The merger was agreed in 2022 and enacted through a 2023 amendment to Japan's national university law. Its headquarters are on the former Tokyo Tech campus at Ookayama, Meguro.
1789110d-d2fe-546a-bb76-da8fc3c966d6.motto: Advancing science and human wellbeing (English form)

dcc6acda-25aa-53c1-82a2-29b74ad8734f.history: KIT was formed on 1 October 2009 by merging the University of Karlsruhe, founded as a polytechnic school in 1825 on the model of the Paris École polytechnique, with the Karlsruhe Research Center, founded as a nuclear research center in 1956. It is both a state university and a national research center of the Helmholtz Association. In 1984 the university received Germany's first email.

4257293d-ae04-50f0-a670-a46ee48a8e44.history: The University of Zurich was founded in 1833 by the canton of Zurich, which combined existing schools of theology, law and medicine with a new faculty of philosophy. It was one of the earliest European universities established by a democratic state rather than by a monarch or the church, and it admitted its first woman student, Nadezhda Suslova, in 1867. Today it is Switzerland's largest university, with seven faculties spread over city-centre and Irchel campuses.

35a032fc-f24f-5a50-92ed-b818fca7f222.history: University College Dublin traces its origins to the Catholic University of Ireland, founded in 1854 with John Henry Newman as its first rector. It became University College Dublin within the National University of Ireland in 1908 and later moved from the city centre to its Belfield campus in south Dublin. It is now Ireland's largest university, with a sizeable international student body and overseas teaching operations.

bfa7cdcc-650a-54d9-baa6-0eaeaa6428a9.history: POSTECH was established in December 1986 with backing from the steel company POSCO, as Korea's first university designed around research from the outset. Its first 249 undergraduates entered in March 1987. The Pohang Accelerator Laboratory's light source was completed on campus in 1994, and the university became a separate legal corporation in 1995. It remains a small, science- and engineering-focused institution with more graduate than undergraduate students.

2eeda25f-2732-523e-b485-bab01ce33cd6.history: Tohoku University was established in Sendai in 1907 as Tohoku Imperial University, the third of Japan's imperial universities. In 1913 it became the first Japanese university to admit women students. It is now a national university with campuses across Sendai and strong programmes in materials science, engineering and disaster science.

48429a40-059c-538c-ad95-c91c68b9cb1c.history: Utrecht University was founded in 1636, growing out of an earlier illustrious school in the city. Over the 20th century it spread from historic buildings in the city centre to the Utrecht Science Park (De Uithof) on the eastern edge of town. It is one of the largest universities in the Netherlands and covers the full range of academic disciplines, with notable research in the geosciences, life sciences and veterinary medicine.

3d2122dd-542a-5bad-94e8-33090f53f6ad.history: Queen Mary University of London was formed through mergers of several older colleges. Its oldest part, the London Hospital Medical College, opened in 1785; others include St Bartholomew's Hospital Medical College (1843), Westfield College (1882) and the People's Palace technical schools in the East End (1887). Queen Mary and Westfield merged in 1989, the two medical colleges joined in 1995, and the name Queen Mary University of London was adopted in 2000. Its main campus is at Mile End in east London.

f7aaf172-d973-5248-b3d6-83289c7c7451.history: RWTH Aachen opened in 1870 as the Royal Rhenish-Westphalian Polytechnic School, set up to train engineers for the industrial Rhineland. Over time it added natural sciences, medicine, humanities and economics, though engineering remains its core. It is now one of Germany's largest technical universities, and more than a third of its students hold foreign citizenship.

39a0a410-8dec-5d39-bba7-99eb9fd534c4.history: Moscow University was founded in 1755 according to a plan by the scholar Mikhail Lomonosov, opening with faculties of philosophy, law and medicine. It grew into a centre of Russian intellectual life in the 19th century and was named after Lomonosov in 1940. Its well-known main building on the Sparrow (Lenin) Hills opened in 1953. Today it is a large public university covering sciences, humanities and social sciences.

35ce761b-adcc-5c73-8bc4-a358b418afa6.history: DTU was founded on 5 November 1829 by the physicist Hans Christian Ørsted as the Polytechnic College (Den Polytekniske Læreanstalt), and Ørsted led it until his death in 1851. It later moved from central Copenhagen to a large campus in Kongens Lyngby north of the city. It is Denmark's main technical university, covering engineering and the technical and natural sciences, with a focus on applied research and start-up support.

dce3ec59-808e-5353-8d69-da5e8e8e29fe.history: King Saud University opened in 1957 in Riyadh as the first university in Saudi Arabia, originally named Riyadh University, with a first class of 21 students in its College of Arts. Women were admitted from the early 1960s, and the institution took the name King Saud University in 1982. It has since grown into a large public university with colleges in sciences, engineering, medicine and humanities, including a separate female campus.

ea07bd5a-d5e8-59b9-bfd9-600587605f25.history: The University of São Paulo was created by the São Paulo state government in 1934, bringing together existing professional schools, including a law school dating from 1827, under a new faculty of philosophy, sciences and letters. It is funded by the state of São Paulo and charges no tuition. It runs campuses in the capital and in cities such as Ribeirão Preto, São Carlos, Piracicaba and Bauru, and is Brazil's largest research university.
ea07bd5a-d5e8-59b9-bfd9-600587605f25.motto: Scientia vinces (With science you will conquer)

dba5fd6f-9afd-5011-aab8-7d0e6cb6ac2a.history: Sungkyunkwan traces its history to 1398, when it opened under the Joseon dynasty as the kingdom's highest Confucian academy for training scholar-officials. It was converted into a modern institution in the late 19th century and re-established as a private university after Korea's liberation. Since 1996 the Samsung group has been part of its foundation. It operates a humanities and social sciences campus in Seoul and a natural sciences campus in Suwon.
dba5fd6f-9afd-5011-aab8-7d0e6cb6ac2a.motto: 修己治人 / 수기치인 (Cultivate oneself and lead others)

04cf5b15-066c-5320-848e-44bd11bb8aa8.history: Qatar's first higher-education institution, a College of Education, was set up by Emiri decree in 1973 with 57 male and 93 female students. Qatar University itself was established in 1977 with four colleges: education, humanities and social sciences, sharia and law, and science. Engineering followed in 1980 and business and economics in 1985. It is the country's national public university, with campuses in Doha.

a3e5ea6a-0e01-58d9-918a-9d90e12e575b.history: The University of Wisconsin was founded in 1848, the year Wisconsin became a state, and held its first classes in February 1849. As the state's land-grant university, it developed the 'Wisconsin Idea' that university research should serve the whole state. It is the flagship of the Universities of Wisconsin system, with a large lakeside campus in Madison.

21e26f0d-fd30-521e-a9f3-fb97b8452d78.history: Sapienza was founded in 1303 by Pope Boniface VIII as the Studium Urbis, Rome's first university. It was later reorganised by the papacy and took the name 'Sapienza' in the 17th century. After Italian unification it became a state university, and in 1935 it moved to the purpose-built Città Universitaria campus. It is one of the largest universities in Europe by enrolment.

accccabf-7374-575c-a90e-2a1b27d4a6ba.history: Teaching at St Andrews began around 1410, and the university received its founding papal bull in 1413, making it Scotland's first university and the third oldest in the English-speaking world. It is a small university in a coastal town, organised around historic colleges such as St Salvator's and St Mary's. A large share of its students come from outside the UK.

sources.label: Founded 1413 (input had 1410, when teaching began); 10,356 students in 2024-25

808b96a5-0e59-5215-a2f5-e7c3c5d2785a.history: The University of Waterloo opened in 1957 with 74 engineering students enrolled in a co-operative programme that alternated study terms with paid work terms. It received its own act of incorporation in 1959 and grew quickly in mathematics, computer science and engineering. Co-operative education remains central to the university, which has one of the largest co-op programmes in the world.
808b96a5-0e59-5215-a2f5-e7c3c5d2785a.motto: Concordia cum veritate (In harmony with truth)

dfd28fce-cef1-56e7-bc57-4cffd211a117.history: Aalto University began operating on 1 January 2010 after the Finnish government merged the Helsinki University of Technology, the Helsinki School of Economics and the University of Art and Design Helsinki. The merger was intended to combine technology, business and design in one institution. Its main campus is in Otaniemi, Espoo, where many buildings were designed by the architect Alvar Aalto, after whom the university is named.

5374c3c7-b54c-5f3e-bc82-39b7babedccf.history: UC Davis began as the University Farm, created by the California legislature in 1905 as the agricultural branch of the University of California; it began enrolling students in 1908. It became a general campus of the UC system in 1959 and added schools of law, medicine and management. It is known for agriculture, veterinary medicine and environmental sciences.

sources.label: Fall 2025 total enrolment 40,617 (incl. residents and interns)

07cc0745-98d8-50c4-8c7d-88b03da6fa79.history: The Pontifical Catholic University of Chile was founded on 21 June 1888, when Archbishop Mariano Casanova of Santiago issued the decree opening the Catholic University. It later received pontifical status from the Holy See. It is a private Catholic university that receives some public funding and has campuses in Santiago and in Villarrica in southern Chile.
07cc0745-98d8-50c4-8c7d-88b03da6fa79.motto: In Christi lumine pro mundi vita (In the light of Christ for the life of the world)

sources.label: Founding decree 21 June 1888 by Archbishop Casanova

ed5b15cb-d889-50df-941c-4764af80621d.history: The University of Helsinki was founded in 1640 as the Royal Academy of Turku, during Swedish rule. After a fire destroyed much of Turku in 1827, it moved to Helsinki, the new capital of the Grand Duchy of Finland, and it took its current name in 1919. It is Finland's oldest and largest university, with four campuses in Helsinki.

sources.label: Cross-check: Royal Academy of Turku, move to Helsinki

29fa6116-cea2-5702-96ea-0f26492434fe.history: IIT Delhi began as the College of Engineering and Technology, whose foundation stone was laid by Prince Philip in 1959 and which opened in August 1961 with support from the British government and industry. In 1963 it was declared an Institution of National Importance and renamed the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi, gaining the right to award its own degrees. Its campus is in Hauz Khas, south Delhi.

710661ab-60ec-57bf-84bc-aa0b1e256a12.history: Leiden University was founded in 1575 by William of Orange, reportedly as a reward to the city for withstanding a Spanish siege, and is the oldest university in the Netherlands. It became an important centre of learning in the Dutch Golden Age. Today it has seven faculties and campuses in both Leiden and The Hague.

80c3fb62-6c22-5ddf-8fe8-841a0a0219b1.history: Rice University was established with the fortune of the Houston merchant William Marsh Rice, who was murdered in 1900 before it opened. It welcomed its first students in 1912 as the William Marsh Rice Institute and was renamed Rice University in 1960. It is a private research university in Houston organised around a residential college system.

10ca55e3-9e48-58e7-a474-d1fab4ccccdb.history: The University of Oslo was founded in 1811 as the Royal Frederick University, named after King Frederick VI of Denmark-Norway, and started teaching in 1813. It was Norway's only university for more than a century and took the name University of Oslo in 1939. Most of its activity is now on the Blindern campus in Oslo.

sources.label: 27,400 students in 2025; committed to education since 1811

0271ce81-bdd1-5aa5-923d-fc97549fa720.history: RMIT began in 1887 as the Working Men's College of Melbourne, founded by the pastoralist and politician Francis Ormond to provide evening technical education. It became the Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology and gained university status in 1992. Today it is a large public university offering both higher and vocational education, with its main campus in central Melbourne and campuses in Vietnam.
0271ce81-bdd1-5aa5-923d-fc97549fa720.motto: Perita manus, mens exculta (A skilled hand, a cultivated mind)

72c8eb2c-4178-5106-b3c2-a72e73dc074c.history: Georgia Tech was created by the Georgia legislature in 1885 as the Georgia School of Technology, part of an effort to industrialise the post-Civil War South, and held its first classes in 1888. It was renamed the Georgia Institute of Technology in 1948. It is a public research university in midtown Atlanta, with a large share of its students in engineering and computing and a fast-growing online graduate programme.

a75ede9d-f2a9-5169-837d-38e810d35a6b.history: The University of Bologna traditionally dates its founding to 1088 and is regarded as the oldest university in continuous operation in the Western world. It grew from independent schools of law, and in 1158 Emperor Frederick I's Constitutio Habita protected travelling scholars. It now operates as a multi-campus university with sites in Bologna, Cesena, Forlì, Ravenna and Rimini, and it gave its name to the Bologna Process for European higher education.
a75ede9d-f2a9-5169-837d-38e810d35a6b.motto: Petrus ubique pater legum Bononia mater (Peter is everywhere the father of the law, Bologna its mother)

d83e0119-d533-524d-a890-6b7c91c8de71.history: The University of Bath received its royal charter in 1966. Its roots go back to a Bristol trade school of 1856, which later became the Bristol College of Science and Technology before moving to Bath. The university is based on a single campus at Claverton Down above the city and is known for engineering, management and sport science, with many courses offering a placement year.
d83e0119-d533-524d-a890-6b7c91c8de71.motto: Generatim discite cultus (Learn each field of study according to its kind)

04c4aef9-ef8e-5981-ba20-50039aeceef5.history: Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (the National University of Malaysia) was founded on 18 May 1970 to provide university education in the Malay language. It opened in Kuala Lumpur with 192 undergraduates and two postgraduates in science, arts and Islamic studies. The move to its main campus in Bangi, Selangor began in 1977, and it was named a research university in 2006 and given autonomous status in 2012.

c770e637-838e-5f90-ae57-425b587061a0.history: Macquarie University was established by an act of the New South Wales parliament in 1964 and began teaching in 1967. It is named after Lachlan Macquarie, an early governor of the colony. Its parkland campus in north-west Sydney sits next to the Macquarie Park business district and includes a private teaching hospital.

It grew into Denmark's second-oldest and one of its largest universities, centred on a yellow-brick park campus in Aarhus. A 2007 merger brought in several research institutes and business and education schools.

b865e086-9fba-5fd2-8b1f-9be60d97baf4.history: Universiti Sains Malaysia was founded in 1969 in Penang as Malaysia's second university, under the name Universiti Pulau Pinang. It began in temporary premises and in 1971 moved to its permanent Minden campus. It was recognised as a research university in 2007 and in 2008 became the first Malaysian university chosen for the government's APEX excellence programme. It also has health and engineering campuses elsewhere in the country.

f68b940c-61ed-5be0-96e9-d70422a3f8bf.history: IIT Bombay was founded in 1958 as the second Indian Institute of Technology and the first set up with foreign help, receiving equipment and experts through UNESCO with funds from the Soviet Union. Its first 100 students began classes in Worli in July 1958 before it moved to its campus at Powai in Mumbai. An act of parliament in 1961 declared it an Institution of National Importance.

d2dff4b3-070b-59d5-a6fb-a12c7095d63b.history: Humboldt University was founded in 1810 as the University of Berlin, following educational ideas associated with Wilhelm von Humboldt that combined teaching and research. It later took the name Friedrich Wilhelm University, and was renamed after the Humboldt brothers in 1949, when it lay in East Berlin. After German reunification it was restructured, and it remains a large university in central Berlin.

5f90631a-ee6a-587d-a542-5fb1d07d0705.history: The University of Science and Technology of China was founded in Beijing in 1958 by the Chinese Academy of Sciences to train scientists for national priorities. In 1970 it moved to Hefei in Anhui province. In 1978 it opened China's first graduate school and its first special class for gifted young students. It remains closely linked to the Academy and is known for physics, quantum science and its national laboratories.

cf17178b-4486-5b1c-84d1-1ef2b3ac9e37.history: Universiti Putra Malaysia started in 1931 as a School of Agriculture in Serdang, Selangor. It became the Malayan College of Agriculture in 1947 and was raised to university status as Universiti Pertanian Malaysia (Agricultural University of Malaysia) in 1971. In 1997 it took its current name to reflect a wider range of subjects, though agriculture and related sciences remain central.

It gained autonomy from the government in 1929. Its main campus, Ciudad Universitaria in Mexico City, was built in the 1950s and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. UNAM also runs secondary schools (bachillerato) and is one of the largest universities in the Americas by enrolment.

It received its royal charter and university status in 1955. It is based mainly on the Streatham campus in Exeter, with further campuses in Exeter and at Penryn in Cornwall.

59063bbd-5451-5ae4-8f6b-b04ebf2c2161.history: Newcastle University traces its origins to a School of Medicine and Surgery founded in Newcastle in 1834 and a College of Physical Science founded in 1871. Both became part of the federal University of Durham and merged in 1937 to form King's College. In 1963 King's College became the independent University of Newcastle upon Tyne. It also runs campuses in Singapore and Malaysia.

It joined the federal Victoria University in 1884 and became an independent university by royal charter in 1903. Its Victoria Building inspired the term 'red brick university'.

835b45a6-e652-5e5e-937b-c365bb1d8e7a.history: Eindhoven University of Technology was founded in 1956 as the Technische Hogeschool Eindhoven, the Netherlands' second technical college, to supply engineers for the growing industry around Philips. It gained full university status and its current name in 1986. Its compact campus in central Eindhoven sits in the high-tech 'Brainport' region.

a8fd79a0-46d7-50c9-aa2f-2fc4d85d493e.history: Erasmus University Rotterdam began in 1913 as the Netherlands School of Commerce, a private initiative backed by Rotterdam's business community. It became the Netherlands School of Economics in 1939, and in 1973 it merged with the Rotterdam medical faculty (founded 1966) to form Erasmus University. It was the first Dutch university named after a person, the humanist Desiderius Erasmus.

d445d34a-9eee-5fcf-8175-3cd18d2f9803.history: The University of Vienna was founded in 1365 by Duke Rudolf IV and is the oldest university in today's German-speaking world. Its main building on the Ringstrasse opened in 1884. It is now one of the largest universities in Central Europe, with about 20 faculties and centres across many sites in Vienna.

55f4ba6f-3df3-5ee2-ac3a-d6e9e0a2b2fa.history: Western University was founded in London, Ontario in 1878 as the Western University of London Ontario, led by Anglican Bishop Isaac Hellmuth. It later became non-denominational and moved to its current campus by the Thames River in the 1920s. Today it is a large public research university with professional schools in business, medicine and law.

6a8b9f04-d032-5a2a-9223-599461b45314.history: Texas A&M opened in College Station in 1876 as the Agricultural and Mechanical College of Texas, the state's first public institution of higher education, created under the federal land-grant program. Military training through the Corps of Cadets was required for students until 1965. It took the name Texas A&M University in 1963 and has grown into one of the largest universities in the United States.

b83472eb-1a12-5b42-9769-79e2649e9009.history: TU Berlin was re-established in 1946, in the British sector of Berlin, as the successor to the Royal Technical College of Charlottenburg. Its roots go back to the Mining Academy (1770), the Building Academy (1799) and the Trade Academy (1821). On reopening it added humanities and social sciences to its engineering subjects. It is one of Germany's larger technical universities, with its main campus in Charlottenburg.

ce0c7503-d037-57dc-98ed-2818fa72fe75.history: The University of Southern California opened in 1880 in what was then a small Los Angeles, with land donated by local backers and a Methodist connection that it later dropped. It is the oldest private research university in California. Its main University Park campus lies near downtown Los Angeles, and it is known for its film, engineering, business and health sciences schools.

98208ca6-3d01-5ce9-b57c-d1724f5ebdab.history: Tongji traces its history to 1907, when the German doctor Erich Paulun founded a German medical school in Shanghai; an engineering school was added in 1912. It became a university in 1923 and National Tongji University in 1927. After the national restructuring of 1952 it focused on civil engineering and architecture, and since 1978 it has grown into a comprehensive university while keeping close ties with Germany.

a002ead6-250c-572d-8773-015f9419b016.history: Stockholm University began in 1878 as Stockholm University College (Stockholms högskola), a private alternative to the traditional universities, which gained the right to award degrees in 1904. It became a state university in 1960 and moved to the Frescati campus north of central Stockholm in the 1970s. It is one of Sweden's largest universities, focused on the sciences, humanities, social sciences and law.
